card.problem_text:
Linear elasticity model (Section 2): general 2D formulation, no specific numerical example.
Geometry: A general 2D domain Ω ⊂ R2 whose boundary is split into a displacement part and a traction part. The section gives no specific shape or dimensions.
Material: Linear elastic material following Hooke's law. In the isotropic case it is described by Young's modulus E and Poisson's ratio ν, through the Lamé constants λ and μ. The section gives no values. This is small-strain linear elasticity, not hyperelasticity.
Boundary conditions: General mixed boundary conditions: prescribed displacement u0 on ∂Ωu and prescribed traction t on ∂Ωσ, with the two parts assumed not to overlap. The section does not say which edges carry which condition.
Loading: General body force f and boundary traction t. The section gives no specific load magnitudes or distributions.
Discretisation in the paper: Not stated. The section derives only the continuous weak form and gives no mesh, element type or element count.

spec.name: General 2D small-strain linear elasticity, mixed BVP (Section 2 continuous weak form, no numerical example)
spec.geometry: General bounded 2D domain Ω ⊂ R^2 with boundary ∂Ω = ∂Ω_u ∪ ∂Ω_σ (no overlap). Shape, dimensions, corners and the location of the Dirichlet/Neumann split are not specified.
spec.material: Linear elastic (Hooke's law), small strain; isotropic case given by E, ν (equivalently Lamé λ, μ). No values given. Not hyperelastic; no geometric or material nonlinearity.
spec.loading: General body force f in Ω, prescribed traction t on ∂Ω_σ, prescribed displacement u0 on ∂Ω_u. No magnitudes or distributions given. Linear problem, so the load level plays no role (no limit points or bifurcation).
well_posedness: Existence and uniqueness (Lax–Milgram plus Korn's inequality) need ∂Ω_u to have positive measure and to remove all rigid-body modes (2 translations and 1 rotation in 2D). If ∂Ω_u is empty (pure traction problem), f and t must be in global force and moment equilibrium, and the solution is unique only up to a rigid-body motion.

Material stability: μ > 0 and λ + μ > 0 in plane strain (equivalently E > 0 and -1 < ν < 0.5). For plane stress the condition is E > 0, -1 < ν < 1 in the 2D constitutive law. As ν → 0.5 (nearly incompressible), standard displacement Q4/T3 elements lock, so stress and displacement convergence degrade unless reduced integration or a mixed formulation is used.
Plane strain versus plane stress is not stated. This changes the effective constitutive law and therefore every QoI value.

Data regularity: f ∈ L2 (or H^-1), t ∈ H^-1/2(∂Ω_σ), u0 ∈ H^1/2(∂Ω_u) give an H^1 weak solution. Higher regularity, and the optimal O(h^2) L2 / O(h) H1 rates for Q4, also need smooth data and a smooth or convex domain without singular points.

Singular features decide which QoIs can converge pointwise. Points where ∂Ω_u meets ∂Ω_σ (clamped–free transition), re-entrant corners, cracks, or jumps in t give singular or near-singular stress. There, peak or pointwise stress may not converge under refinement, while strain energy, displacements and region-averaged stresses still do (at reduced rates).
Linear problem: no load-level limit points, buckling or loss of ellipticity. Solution uniqueness depends only on the boundary conditions and material constants above.
open_questions: The question's list of candidate reference quantities is empty ('which of these quantities ... : ?'). Which QoIs should be assessed, e.g. strain energy, tip or point displacement, reaction force, peak von Mises stress, region-averaged stress?
No specific geometry, dimensions or corner angles are given, so the presence of re-entrant corners or cracks cannot be determined.
It is not stated which edges are ∂Ω_u and which are ∂Ω_σ, or whether the Dirichlet part removes all rigid-body modes. Clamped–free junctions, and therefore stress singularities, cannot be ruled out.
No values are given for E and ν. Nearness to incompressibility (locking risk) is unknown.
Plane strain or plane stress is not specified.
No magnitudes or distributions are given for f, t or u0, including whether t has discontinuities.
Discretisation is not stated: element type, mesh, refinement strategy. Q4 is a placeholder because the schema requires a value. The paper gives no element.
No exact or manufactured solution is given. The reference type is assumed to be a mesh-refinement family unless the paper later supplies a manufactured solution.
The problem is described as part of a hyperelasticity verification pipeline but is small-strain linear elasticity. Is it intended as the linearized limit or baseline for later nonlinear examples?

steps.detail: The problem describes only the general continuous formulation of small-strain linear elasticity (Section 2) and has no concrete instance. It gives no domain shape or dimensions, so no cell union can be built. It does not say which boundary segments carry the displacement condition and which carry the traction condition. It gives no values for E, ν, the body force f, the prescribed displacement u0 or the traction t. It names no points or quantities of interest, and the question's list of quantities is empty. Any geometry, boundary condition or load I chose would be invented rather than taken from the problem, so the result could not be traced back to the source. For the same reason, none of the quantities can be offered as trustworthy reference values. The general formulation itself (Hooke's law with Lamé constants and mixed displacement/traction boundary conditions) does fit the pipeline. A specific numerical example with stated geometry, boundary conditions, material values and loads would be needed before it can be formalized.
